exercise.name: Dumbbell Overhead Carry

reference.title: Dumbbell Single Arm Overhead Carry
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Weightlifting, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (isometric overhead shoulder stability and trunk bracing while walking)

breathing.pattern: Brace and keep breathing in short, steady breaths behind the brace.
breathing.cadence: Slow, controlled steps (about 80 a minute here)

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbell you can hold locked out overhead for the whole distance (lighter than for a farmers carry)
prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbell, longer distance, or two dumbbells overhead

cues.text: Press or clean the dumbbell overhead: arm locked, biceps by the ear, dumbbell over the shoulder, free arm relaxed.
Walk slowly and tall; ribs down, no leaning away from the weight.
Stop with the feet together, then lower the dumbbell to the shoulder under control.

mistakes.fix: Ribs down and glutes tight; use a lighter dumbbell.

mistakes.mistake: Dumbbell drifting forward or behind the head
mistakes.fix: Stack wrist, elbow and shoulder; biceps by the ear.
Lock the elbow and push up into the dumbbell.

kinematics.setup: Upper arm ≈170° from the trunk, elbow ≈14°
kinematics.peak: Dumbbell within 3.3 cm (horizontally) of the shoulder joint while walking
kinematics.norm: Arm straight with the dumbbell stacked over the shoulder (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 50 cm steps, 100 cm per loop, 0.75 s per step
kinematics.norm: Slow, controlled steps (clinical opinion; Taylor & Reed 2020 cue slow, controlled walking for carries)
Upright with no side bend (Taylor & Reed 2020)

sources.title: GymVisual #354812, Dumbbell Single Arm Overhead Carry, video (movement reference)
Taylor & Reed 2020, increase hip and trunk stability with loaded carries for injury prevention, rehabilitation, and performance (NSCA Coach 7(3))
The quantification of muscle activation during the loaded carry movement pattern, 2024 (Int J Exerc Sci 17(1):480-490; PubMed 38665162)
McGill & Marshall 2012, kettlebell swing, snatch, and bottoms-up carry: back and hip muscle activation, motion, and low back loads (J Strength Cond Res 26(1):16-27)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The dumbbell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Shoulder pain or limited overhead mobility: choose a farmers or front-rack carry instead.
If the lockout fails, bring the dumbbell down to the shoulder or step away from it; never let it fall over the head.
modify: Limited overhead mobility: use a lighter dumbbell or a bottoms-up or rack carry (McGill 2012 studied carries in the rack and bottoms-up positions).
progressions: Mixed carry: one dumbbell overhead, one at the side.

muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Shrug the shoulder blade up to support the lockout.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blade up so the arm can stay overhead without pinching.
muscleNotes.core: Brace so the ribs do not flare and the trunk does not bend away from the weight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Keeps the dumbbell from drifting behind the head.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Steadies the shoulder; overhead carries challenge the shoulder stabilisers (Taylor & Reed 2020).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist side bending under the one-sided load (asymmetric carries added ipsilateral trunk activity in the suitcase carry, Int J Exerc Sci 2024).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist side bending under the one-sided load (asymmetric carries added ipsilateral trunk activity in the suitcase carry, Int J Exerc Sci 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on each step.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level on each step.
